records.title: Why a conceptual model first
records.text: One-order-one-shipment is encoded in several places: `OrderStatus.Shipped`, the notification topics, and `Shipment.carrier` as a free-text string. Agreeing the concepts before touching the types avoids a second migration. The OntoUML diagram is the working artefact for this discussion; it is a draft, not a specification.

records.title: Participants
records.text:
- **Settled**: An order is between a customer and the seller. The seller is always Northwind today; modelling it as a role keeps marketplace sellers possible without promising them.
- **Settled**: A shipment belongs to exactly one order and leaves from exactly one warehouse. An order has zero or more shipments.
- **Proposed**: A carrier is optional until dispatch, because an allocated shipment has none yet. Parcels exist from packing onwards.

records.title: Shipment lifecycle
records.text:
Allocated → Packed → In transit → Delivered. The phases are exclusive and every shipment is in exactly one of them.
- **Added 2026-10-07**: Delivery failed, when the carrier has stopped trying (bad address, refused). What happens next is open question 1.

records.title: Order status
records.text:
Open → Partially shipped → Fulfilled, or Cancelled. Derived from the order's shipments, never set directly.
- Partially shipped: at least one shipment is in transit or delivered and some lines have no shipment yet.

records.title: Split shipments
records.text:
- **Proposed**: Split only by warehouse, never within one warehouse: at most one shipment per warehouse per order.
- **Settled**: Shipping is charged once per order, however many shipments it takes.

records.title: Open questions
records.text:
1. After a failed delivery, is the redelivery the same shipment (back to In transit) or a new one? This decides tracking-number history and whether work-0003 sends a second "dispatched" email.
2. Can the unshipped rest of a partially shipped order be cancelled, and is that order then Fulfilled or Cancelled?
3. Can a parcel move to a different shipment (re-packed after damage at the dock)? If so, a parcel's shipment isn't fixed.
4. Is Picking a phase we need here, or only a state inside the warehouse system?

records.title: Order
records.text: A customer's purchase from the seller, covering one or more order lines.

records.title: Seller
records.text: The organisation an order is placed with. Currently always Northwind.

records.title: Partially shipped
records.text: An order with at least one dispatched shipment and lines that have no shipment yet.

records.title: Shipment
records.text: Goods for one order that leave one warehouse together.

records.title: Parcel
records.text: A physical package within a shipment, carrying its own carrier label.

records.title: Carrier
records.text: The organisation that transports a shipment once it is dispatched.

records.title: Warehouse
records.text: A Northwind stock location that ships to customers.

records.title: Split shipment
records.text: An order fulfilled by more than one shipment.

records.title: Delivery failed
records.text: A shipment the carrier could not deliver and has stopped attempting.

order.rationale: Exists in shop as Order; modelled as the relation between a customer and the seller rather than a record.

shipment.rationale: A shipment depends on exactly one order and one warehouse; carrier and parcels arrive later in its life.

questions.question: Is a redelivery after Delivery Failed the same shipment?
questions.why: Decides whether Delivery Failed can transition back to In Transit.

shipment-carrier.rationale: 0..1 because allocated and packed shipments have no carrier yet. In Transit and Delivered always have one; this model can't say that without phase-specific relations.

seller.rationale: Always Northwind today; a role so marketplace sellers stay possible.

walkthroughs.title: How one order becomes several shipments

steps.text: An order relates exactly one customer and the seller. It exists before anything ships.
Each shipment fulfils one order and leaves one warehouse. An order with stock in Berlin and Leeds gets two shipments.
Carrier and parcels are optional on the shipment side: an allocated shipment has neither yet.
Every shipment is in exactly one phase. The order's phase follows from its shipments.
